correctness.rationale: For Z=(oplus_gamma X_gamma)_{c0} with dual (oplus X_gamma*)_{ell1}, fix any global slice and any coordinate gamma0. A finite-support witness, norming all but an arbitrarily small dual l1 tail and making component gamma0 arbitrarily far in its own slice, yields dc_Z(x)>=dc_gamma0(x_gamma0). If the selected dual coordinate vanishes, an opposite norm-one vector gives distance 1+||x_gamma0||, still above dc_gamma0. For the reverse, approximate x by finitely many non-small coordinates and combine their near-optimal component slice functionals with positive weights into a single norm-one global functional; a small deficit forces every selected component slice. Outside this finite set c0 gives ||x_gamma||<epsilon, and for infinite Gamma the needed M=sup dc_gamma(x_gamma)>=1 is proved from dc_gamma(y)>=1-||y|| along vanishing tail. Finite Gamma works without tail. Thus exact supremum formula holds for all real Banach-valued c0 sums. No finite numeric experiment substitutes for proof.
